item.title: What If You Could Experience Venice Carnival From the Inside?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Venice Carnival takes on a more intimate character at Violino d’Oro, where guests can experience one of Italy’s most celebrated traditions through local craftsmanship, private access and insider connections. Located in the heart of Venice, the hotel is offering a Carnival experience from January 30 through February 9 that begins with a visit to a Venetian atelier and a meeting with local designer Antonia Sautter. Guests can learn about the artistry behind the costumes before selecting a customized, made-to-measure Carnival dress, with Violino d’Oro arranging the fittings, water taxi transfers and access to one of Venice’s prestigious themed Carnival balls.

The experience continues beyond the costume with private entry to Palazzo Ducale and the prisons associated with Casanova’s famous escape, tea at the historic Caffè Florian, and a masked photoshoot through Venice’s canals aboard a gondola. Guests can also take part in a cocktail class at Il Piccolo Bar, creating an itinerary that connects the spectacle of Carnival with the craftsmanship, history and traditions of Venice itself. Rather than simply attending Carnival, the experience offers travelers the opportunity to encounter the festival through the people and places that give it its distinctive character.

The Curated Take: What makes this experience compelling is the access behind the spectacle. Carnival is one of Venice’s most recognizable traditions, but Violino d’Oro builds an itinerary around the creative process and local relationships that exist beneath the masks and costumes. Meeting a Venetian designer, commissioning a personalized look and gaining access to historic and cultural sites creates a more layered way to experience Venice during Carnival, particularly for luxury travelers who value craftsmanship, storytelling and connections with the destination.

item.title: What Happens When an Alpine Ski Resort Becomes a Winter Wellness Retreat?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Winter at Forsthofgut Nature Hotel in Leogang, Austria, extends well beyond the ski slopes. Set in the Austrian Alps with ski-in/ski-out access to the Saalbach Hinterglemm Leogang Fieberbrunn ski area, the luxury nature hotel puts guests within reach of approximately 168 miles of slopes while also offering snowshoeing, tobogganing and a new ice rink debuting this winter. The experience shifts indoors after a day in the snow, where the expansive 61,000-square-foot waldSPA features panoramic saunas, indoor and outdoor pools and an onsen-style pool overlooking the surrounding landscape.

Wellness is equally central to the resort’s winter offering. At waldSPA Health, guests can explore treatments and experiences including cryotherapy and altitude training, while the Mountain Loft Suites provide a more secluded retreat with private terraces, saunas and hot tubs overlooking the snow-covered Leoganger Steinberge. The result is an Alpine escape that pairs the active pleasures of winter in Leogang, Austria, with the increasingly sought-after luxury of having somewhere restorative to retreat when the day outside is done.

The Curated Take: Forsthofgut is interesting because it treats winter as more than a season for skiing. The combination of access to a major Alpine ski area, an unusually expansive spa, specialized wellness experiences and private suites with their own saunas and hot tubs gives travelers multiple ways to experience the mountains. For luxury travelers who want the drama of the Austrian Alps without spending every hour on the slopes, that balance of adventure, nature and restoration is part of the appeal.

item.title: What If You Could Have a Swiss Mountain All to Yourself?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
High above Lake St. Moritz in St. Moritz, Switzerland, the five-star, all-suite Carlton Hotel St. Moritz offers a winter escape built around both the glamour and the quieter pleasures of the Engadine. Guests can explore the snowy landscape by horse-drawn carriage, husky sled, ice skate across the frozen lake or venture out with the hotel’s Outdoor Butler, who can arrange everything from a personalized ski tour to a snow trek through the surrounding mountains. The resort’s setting also puts travelers within easy reach of the designer boutiques and polished atmosphere of St. Moritz, one of Switzerland’s most renowned winter destinations.

For an experience that takes exclusivity a step further, the hotel’s Rent a Mountain experience gives guests private access to an illuminated ski slope and gondola for an evening on the mountain without the usual crowds. Back at the hotel, the experience can continue with a private Fondue Gondola or time spent unwinding at the Bel Etage. It is a distinctly St. Moritz approach to winter travel: alpine adventure, après-ski indulgence and the kind of privacy that turns a snowy escape into something truly memorable.

The Curated Take: The appeal of Carlton Hotel St. Moritz is not simply its access to winter sports, but the range of ways it allows travelers to experience the Swiss Alps on their own terms. The combination of a personal Outdoor Butler, private mountain access and refined après-ski experiences creates a version of St. Moritz that feels less like checking off a list of winter activities and more like having the landscape arranged around you. For luxury travelers seeking both iconic Alpine scenery and meaningful exclusivity, that distinction is significant.

item.title: Perth Welcomes a New British Pub With The Queen’s Arms
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A traditional British pub is returning to Perth’s CBD with the opening of The Queen’s Arms in a heritage-listed, three-level building on Queen Street. The 500-capacity venue features two bars with more than 30 taps, multiple dining areas, an elevated beer garden and rooftop terrace, with a menu centered on British pub classics alongside Australian favorites. The opening marks the return of a traditional British pub to the heart of Perth after nearly a decade.

The project comes from hospitality group Nokturnl, whose portfolio includes venues at Yagan Square, and gives the city’s evolving dining scene another large-scale social destination. Its combination of historic architecture, pub culture and multiple indoor and outdoor spaces is designed to make it as much a gathering place as a restaurant.

The Curated Take:
The Queen’s Arms is an interesting example of how a city can embrace a familiar cultural idea while giving it a distinctly local setting. The heritage building, Australian ingredients and Perth location keep the concept from feeling like a replica transported wholesale from Britain.

item.title: Perth Mint Creates the World’s Largest Gold Bar
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Perth Mint has claimed a Guinness World Records title with a gold bar weighing an extraordinary 521.2 kilograms and refined to 99.999 percent purity. The record-setting bar represents a technical achievement for the historic mint, which has been operating for 127 years, and adds another remarkable object to its public collection alongside its record-breaking One Tonne Gold Coin.

The bar will become part of The Perth Mint’s Exhibition, giving visitors an opportunity to see an object that combines Australia’s long association with gold with the technical expertise of one of the country’s best-known precious-metals institutions. It is an unexpected addition to Perth’s cultural attractions and an especially striking stop for travelers interested in the history, craftsmanship and industry behind Australia’s gold story.

The Curated Take:
There is a satisfying travel story hiding behind what initially sounds like a novelty record. The world’s largest gold bar connects Perth’s present-day technical capabilities with the city’s deep history as a center of Australia’s gold industry, making it more than simply an enormous piece of precious metal.

item.title: Pearl Expeditions Creates an Ultimate 14-Day Kimberley Journey
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Pearl Expeditions has introduced a new 14-day 2027 itinerary combining luxury lodging, expedition cruising and aerial exploration across Western Australia’s remote Kimberley. The journey begins with two nights at adults-only El Questro Homestead before guests board the boutique expedition yacht Paspaley Pearl for ten nights along the Kimberley coast. Travelers can then add an aerial adventure, choosing between a helicopter flight over Mitchell Falls or a flight aboard Paspaley’s Grumman Mallard flying boats at Kuri Bay, before finishing in Broome.

The itinerary brings together several of the Kimberley’s defining experiences in a single journey, moving from a luxury wilderness lodge to small-ship cruising and finally into Australia’s pearling capital. Rather than treating the Kimberley as a quick excursion, the package is structured around allowing travelers to experience its immense coastline and remote landscapes at a slower pace.

The Curated Take:
The Kimberley rewards travelers willing to make the journey, and this itinerary is built around exactly that idea. Its appeal is the variety of perspectives: wilderness from land, sea and air, with the intimacy of a small expedition vessel and the rare opportunity to experience the region from above.

item.title: Voltage Lodge Turns a Historic Collie Building Into an Adventure Base
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A 90-year-old former co-op storeroom has found a new life in Collie, where Voltage Lodge has opened as a purpose-built accommodation base for travelers exploring Western Australia’s growing adventure scene. Designed for groups, the lodge sleeps up to 30 guests and combines private ensuite rooms with bunk and family accommodations, alongside a communal kitchen and lounge intended to encourage travelers to gather after a day outdoors.

The property is particularly geared toward mountain bikers, with secure storage for up to 30 bikes, e-bike charging, a wash-down bay and repair station. With Collie developing a reputation for its mountain biking and trail network, Voltage Lodge adds accommodation specifically designed around the needs of active travelers while preserving the character of the historic building.

The Curated Take:
There is something compelling about a new hotel that responds directly to the identity of its destination. Voltage Lodge isn’t trying to turn Collie into something it isn’t; it is designed around the forests, trails, rivers and cycling culture that are already drawing visitors there, making the accommodation part of the adventure rather than simply a place to sleep.

item.title: Daytona Beach’s Fall Festival Calendar Celebrates Art, Motorcycles, Cars and Coastal Culture
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From roaring motorcycles and polished classic cars to juried art, Greek traditions and fresh seafood, the Daytona Beach area is embracing fall with a diverse lineup of festivals and special events. The calendar stretches from October through Thanksgiving weekend, offering visitors multiple ways to experience the destination beyond its famous beaches and motorsports heritage.

The season begins with the 34th annual Biketoberfest®, taking place October 15–18, featuring live music, industry vendors, bike shows, motorcycle racing at Daytona International Speedway and scenic rides along routes such as A1A, Main Street and the Ormond Beach Scenic Loop. November brings the 63rd annual Halifax Art Festival, showcasing more than 200 juried artists along the Halifax River, alongside the Greek Festival at St. Demetrios Greek Orthodox Church, where traditional food, music, dancing and crafts celebrate more than four decades of local heritage. The Riverfest Seafood Festival follows November 21–22 in Ormond Beach, while DeLand’s Fall Festival of the Arts presents 150 juried artists in downtown’s historic setting. Closing out the season is the 53rd annual Daytona Turkey Run, November 25–29, where thousands of classic and custom vehicles, automotive parts and memorabilia take over Daytona International Speedway.

The Curated Take

Daytona Beach’s fall festival season reveals a destination with a broader cultural personality than its racing reputation might suggest. The combination of major enthusiast gatherings, established art festivals, community traditions and waterfront food events creates an appealing mix of experiences, whether visitors arrive for a particular passion or simply want to explore the region at a lively time of year. For travelers, the festival calendar also offers a useful reason to venture beyond the beach and discover the distinct character of Daytona Beach, Ormond Beach and DeLand.

item.title: Australia and New Zealand Renew a Classic Cricket Rivalry in Perth
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Perth’s Optus Stadium will host the opening Test of the Chappell-Hadlee Series when Australia takes on New Zealand from December 9–13, 2026. The match marks the return of the trans-Tasman rivalry to Australian shores and will form part of the series continuing into January 2027. Premium hospitality packages will also be available, including signature dining experiences, private suites and outdoor boxes.

For cricket fans, the fixture offers the chance to see two neighboring nations compete in one of the sport’s most familiar rivalries, while Perth provides a distinctive setting for the opening encounter. The stadium’s hospitality options also position the event as an experience that can appeal to travelers looking to combine live sport with a more elevated spectator setting.

The Curated Take:
A Test match offers a different rhythm from many major sporting events, with time to settle into the atmosphere and let the day unfold. For visitors, the Chappell-Hadlee Series provides an opportunity to experience a classic cricket rivalry while enjoying Perth’s modern stadium and broader destination appeal.

item.title: Pair’d Margaret River Region Brings Global Chefs and Local Wine Together
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Margaret River Region’s celebrated food and wine scene will take center stage during Pair’d Margaret River Region, returning November 19–22, 2026. The four-day festival brings together winemakers, chefs, musicians and producers across some of the region’s most distinctive venues, with a program that includes beachside feasts, cellar-door experiences, intimate meals and events celebrating the area’s acclaimed wines.

This year’s lineup includes Michelin-starred chefs Dave Pynt, Matt Abé and Matt Abergel, alongside renowned American pitmaster Rodney Scott. Their participation adds an international dimension to a festival rooted in Margaret River’s own producers and culinary identity. Alongside the visiting talent, the expanded program features music, new events and returning favorites, inviting visitors to experience the region through its food, wine and sense of place.

The Curated Take:
Pair’d is compelling because it treats food and wine as a way of understanding a destination, not simply as a collection of indulgences. The international chef lineup brings fresh perspectives, but the festival’s real draw is the opportunity to experience those collaborations within Margaret River’s vineyards, coastline and local culinary community.
